The **Finance (No. 2) Act 2010** (c. 31) was a UK Act of Parliament that received Royal Assent on **27 July 2010**. It introduced various tax and financial measures following the **June 2010 Budget** (the first Budget of the **Coalition Government** led by David Cameron and Nick Clegg). Below is a detailed breakdown of its key provisions:

---

### **1. Background & Context**
- The Act was introduced to implement tax changes announced in the **June 2010 Budget**, which aimed to reduce the UK's budget deficit while supporting economic recovery post the **2008 financial crisis**.
- It was the second Finance Act of 2010 (the first being the **Finance Act 2010**, which implemented the **March 2010 Budget** under the Labour government).
- The Coalition Government prioritised **fiscal consolidation**, with measures to increase tax revenues and reduce public spending.

---

### **2. Key Tax Changes**
#### **A. Income Tax**
1. **Personal Allowance Increase**
   - The **basic personal allowance** for individuals under 65 was increased from **£6,475 to £7,475** (effective from **6 April 2011**).
   - This was part of a long-term plan to raise the personal allowance to **£10,000** (achieved in 2014).

2. **Higher Rate Threshold Freeze**
   - The **higher rate threshold** (40% tax band) was **frozen at £37,400** (for 2011-12), meaning more people were dragged into the higher rate as wages rose.

3. **Additional Rate (50% Tax Band)**
   - The **50% income tax rate** (for earnings above **£150,000**) introduced by Labour in **Finance Act 2009** was **retained** (though later reduced to **45%** in **Finance Act 2013**).

#### **B. National Insurance Contributions (NICs)**
1. **Increase in NIC Rates**
   - **Employee NICs** increased by **1%** (from **11% to 12%** on earnings between the primary threshold and upper earnings limit).
   - **Employer NICs** increased by **1%** (from **12.8% to 13.8%**).
   - The **upper earnings limit** was aligned with the **higher rate income tax threshold** (£42,475 for 2011-12).

2. **Small Business NIC Relief**
   - A **£21 per week NICs holiday** was introduced for new businesses outside London, the South East, and East of England (to encourage job creation).

#### **C. Value Added Tax (VAT)**
1. **Standard Rate Increase**
   - The **VAT standard rate** was **increased from 17.5% to 20%** (effective from **4 January 2011**).
   - This was a major revenue-raising measure, expected to generate **£13 billion per year**.

2. **Reduced Rate (5%) & Zero Rate**
   - No changes were made to the **5% reduced rate** (e.g., domestic fuel) or **zero-rated items** (e.g., most food, children’s clothes).

#### **D. Capital Gains Tax (CGT)**
1. **Increase in CGT Rates**
   - The **CGT rate for higher-rate taxpayers** was **increased from 18% to 28%** (effective from **23 June 2010**).
   - The **10% entrepreneurs' relief rate** was **retained** (up to a lifetime limit of **£5 million**).

2. **Annual Exempt Amount**
   - The **CGT annual exempt amount** was **frozen at £10,100** (for 2010-11).

#### **E. Corporation Tax**
1. **Main Rate Reduction**
   - The **main corporation tax rate** was **reduced from 28% to 27%** (effective from **1 April 2011**).
   - Further reductions were planned (to **24% by 2014**).

2. **Small Profits Rate**
   - The **small profits rate** (for companies with profits ≤ £300,000) was **reduced from 21% to 20%** (effective from **1 April 2011**).

#### **F. Inheritance Tax (IHT)**
1. **Nil-Rate Band Freeze**
   - The **IHT nil-rate band** was **frozen at £325,000** until **2014-15** (extended later).

#### **G. Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT)**
1. **Increase for High-Value Properties**
   - A new **5% SDLT rate** was introduced for **residential properties over £1 million** (effective from **6 April 2011**).

#### **H. Fuel Duty**
1. **Fuel Duty Increase**
   - Fuel duty was **increased by 1p per litre** (effective from **1 October 2010**).
   - Further increases were planned but later delayed due to public opposition.

#### **I. Alcohol & Tobacco Duties**
1. **Alcohol Duty**
   - **Beer duty** increased by **2%** above inflation.
   - **Wine & spirits duties** increased by **2%** above inflation.

2. **Tobacco Duty**
   - **Tobacco duty** increased by **1%** above inflation.

#### **J. Anti-Avoidance Measures**
1. **Disclosure of Tax Avoidance Schemes (DOTAS)**
   - Strengthened rules to require **earlier disclosure** of tax avoidance schemes.

2. **Targeted Anti-Avoidance Rules (TAARs)**
   - New rules to counter **artificial loss creation** and **tax avoidance via offshore structures**.

3. **Bank Payroll Tax (Repeal)**
   - The **50% bank payroll tax** (introduced in **Finance Act 2010**) was **repealed** (as it was a one-off measure).

---

### **3. Other Key Provisions**
#### **A. Pensions**
1. **Annual Allowance Reduction**
   - The **annual allowance for tax-relieved pension contributions** was **reduced from £255,000 to £50,000** (effective from **6 April 2011**).

2. **Lifetime Allowance Reduction**
   - The **lifetime allowance** was **reduced from £1.8 million to £1.5 million** (effective from **6 April 2012**).

#### **B. Child Benefit**
1. **Freeze on Child Benefit**
   - Child Benefit rates were **frozen for three years** (2011-14).

#### **C. Business & Investment Incentives**
1. **Enterprise Investment Scheme (EIS) & Venture Capital Trusts (VCTs)**
   - **Income tax relief** for EIS investments was **increased from 20% to 30%** (effective from **6 April 2011**).
   - **VCT income tax relief** remained at **30%**.

2. **Research & Development (R&D) Tax Credits**
   - Enhanced relief for **SMEs** (up to **225% of qualifying expenditure**).

#### **D. Environmental Taxes**
1. **Air Passenger Duty (APD)**
   - **APD rates increased** (e.g., long-haul economy flights rose from **£60 to £85**).

2. **Landfill Tax**
   - **Standard rate** increased from **£48 to £56 per tonne** (effective from **1 April 2011**).

---

### **4. Economic & Political Impact**
- **Deficit Reduction**: The Act was part of the Coalition’s **austerity measures**, aiming to reduce the UK’s **£156 billion budget deficit**.
- **Public Reaction**:
  - The **VAT increase to 20%** was controversial, seen as regressive (affecting lower-income households more).
  - The **50% income tax rate** was criticised by businesses as discouraging investment.
  - The **NICs increase** was unpopular with employers.
- **Long-Term Effects**:
  - The **personal allowance increase** helped low-income workers.
  - The **corporation tax cuts** were later credited with attracting businesses to the UK.
  - The **pension allowance reductions** affected high earners.

---

### **5. Subsequent Amendments & Repeals**
- The **50% income tax rate** was **reduced to 45%** in **Finance Act 2013**.
- The **VAT rate (20%)** remained unchanged (as of 2024).
- The **corporation tax rate** was further reduced to **19%** (2017) and later **25%** (2023).
- The **pension annual allowance** was **increased to £60,000** (2023).

---

### **6. Full Text & Legislative History**
- The **Finance (No. 2) Act 2010** can be read in full on the **[UK Legislation website](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2010/31/contents)**.
- It was debated in **Parliament** between **June and July 2010**, with key speeches from:
  - **George Osborne** (Chancellor of the Exchequer)
  - **Alistair Darling** (Shadow Chancellor, Labour)
  - **Vince Cable** (Business Secretary, Lib Dem)

---

### **7. Summary of Key Takeaways**
| **Area**               | **Key Change**                                                                 |
|------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Income Tax**         | Personal allowance ↑ to £7,475; 50% rate retained; higher rate threshold frozen. |
| **NICs**               | Rates ↑ by 1% for employees & employers.                                     |
| **VAT**                | Standard rate ↑ to 20% (from 17.5%).                                          |
| **CGT**                | Higher-rate taxpayers pay 28% (up from 18%).                                 |
| **Corporation Tax**    | Main rate ↓ to 27% (later 19%).                                               |
| **Pensions**           | Annual allowance ↓ to £50,000; lifetime allowance ↓ to £1.5m.                 |
| **SDLT**               | 5% rate for properties > £1m.                                                 |
| **Anti-Avoidance**     | Strengthened DOTAS rules.                                                     |

---

### **8. Further Reading**
- **[HM Treasury – June 2010 Budget](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/budget-2010-documents)**
- **[Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) Analysis](https://ifs.org.uk/)**
- **[UK Parliament – Finance (No. 2) Act 2010 Debates](https://hansard.parliament.uk/)**
